subject: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access, break-glass
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access, break-glass

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery call and a couple of follow-ups so we can scope the next POC:  

1) Primary concerns you raised: PII handling & retention, audit/logging for admin/support actions, and emergency "break-glass" access procedures.  
2) For RBAC: you mentioned wanting role templates mapped to FinTrust org roles (admin, analyst, read-only), and enforced least-privilege for support.  

Can you confirm:  
- Which environments need data residency controls (US-only vs multi-region)?  
- Expected retention window for user content and logs (e.g., 30/90/365 days)?  
- Any mandatory support access workflow (Jira ticket required, approval chain) you want enforced for our Support engineers?  

I'll loop in Dev and Rishi for technical detail — attaching a short brief on Redwood's access control model. Happy to set a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through specifics and an initial mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_Access_Control_Brief.pdf (1 page summary of RBAC, break-glass, support access)

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access, break-glass

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few answers inline:  

- Data residency: for production customer data we require US-only storage for now; backups may be replicated to EU for DR but must be encrypted and access-restricted.  
- Retention: default customer content retention is 90 days; audit logs retained 365 days. We can discuss exceptions for regulatory teams.  
- Support access: must be tied to an internal ticket (ServiceNow) and require manager approval for any elevated access. Break-glass must be logged, reviewed, and require a separate post-incident attestation.  

I've attached our security questionnaire and a short doc describing our support approval workflow. Can your team confirm whether Redwood supports: per-customer RBAC (separate admin roles per account), just-in-time (JIT) elevated access for support, and immutable audit trails for any break-glass events?  

Cheers,
Alex Jones
Director, Security Engineering | FinTrust
alex.jones@fintrust.com

Attachments: FinTrust_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access, break-glass

Thanks Alex — that's helpful. Quick answers from our side:  

- Per-customer RBAC: yes, Redwood supports account-scoped roles and custom role templates that map to customer-defined role names.  
- JIT elevated access: supported via time-limited support tokens and can be gated by both a ServiceNow ticket ID and a manager approval step.  
- Immutable audit trails: we store admin/support action audit logs for 365 days, signed and tamper-evident; break-glass events are flagged and require a post-incident attestation which is retained with the event.  

Dev, can you add a note with the technical references and a short config checklist we can share with FinTrust?

Proposed next steps:  
1) Dev runs a 30-min technical review with FinTrust security to validate JIT + approval flow.  
2) We exchange a draft mutual action plan and scope POC for RBAC + logging.  
3) FinTrust sends the completed questionnaire; we'll respond with evidence for SOC2 / encryption in transit & at rest.  

Alex — would Thursday or Friday morning PST work for the review?

Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintrust.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access, break-glass

Hi Alex — quick technical notes and references:  

- Account-scoped roles: our control plane supports tenant-scoped RBAC. Roles are enforced at the service gateway; tokens carry scoped claims (account_id, role). Role templates can be provisioned via API or Console.  
- JIT support access: implemented as short-lived scoped tokens issued after approval. We support integrating approval webhooks with ServiceNow so the issuance is automated after the manager approval event.  
- Audit & break-glass: audit entries include actor, action, timestamp, request-id, and checksum; break-glass events emit an immutable record and a mandatory post-incident attestation field. Logs are exported to customer-owned S3 or pushed to Splunk/Datadog — retention configurable up to 7 years.  

I'll prepare a 20–30 min demo of the JIT flow and audit export for Thursday 10:00 AM PST. I'll also drop a short configuration checklist and the API reference link here:  
https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/access-control-brief.pdf  

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Access_Control_Config_Checklist.pdf

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintrust.com>

Alex
